reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the critic judged that the reading misread the request: The reading assumes this job "touches no code" and that emptying exempt and deleting records/ need no code change. Both are wrong. The per-commit gate refuses any deleted file under records/ (content.rs:46-61, run on every Athena commit through commits.rs:202 with Scope::Commit). Admission refuses any job change under records/ (admission.rs:695). Gate tests rely on the repo's exempt list being non-empty (lib.rs:443, history.rs:384-840, legacy.rs:481). With crates/ out of scope, criteria 1, 5 and 6 cannot be met. The request needs a prerequisite code job, or a reading that lets code change. (round 1 of 5). I'm rejecting this plan because the request can't be done without changing code, and the reading forbids any code change. The plan says Athena's landing will delete records/, but no code does that. The gate's append-only check refuses any deleted file under records/ (content.rs:46-61). That check runs on every commit Athena makes (commits.rs:202, Scope::Commit), and admission refuses any job change under records/ (admission.rs:695). The design note that the removal "does not trip the append-only rule" covers only the full-history check, not the per-commit gate. The plan also admits that criteria 5 and 6 fail, and I confirmed it: lib.rs:443 and history.rs:384-840 rely on a non-empty exempt list. The planner did surface these conflicts as open questions instead of patching code, which follows the reading. The fix is a prerequisite code job that allows a post-cutover removal of records/ and moves the seven legacy commit ids into test-only helpers. After that, this job can be re-planned as config and docs edits plus a deletion the code allows. The rest checked out: the cited files and line numbers exist, D171 is the next free number, and leaving ci.yml unchanged is justified. Findings: blocker: No mechanism can delete records/ from main. The gate and admission both refuse it, so criterion 1 cannot be met.
